start.name: Abu Madi onshore gas field / gas treatment plant, Kafr El Sheikh area, Nile Delta, Egypt (exact facility location not independently public/geocodable)
start.coord_basis: No public source gives a specific coordinate or named locality for the Abu Madi onshore field/treatment plant. 'Abu Madi' is also used as a geological formation name covering a much wider sub-surface area (including the separate OFFSHORE Baltim fields), so a Baltim-area anchor would risk conflating the onshore 1967 field with an unrelated offshore accumulation — not used for that reason. OpenStreetMap/Nominatim searches for 'Abu Madi' (English and Arabic, various transliterations) return no matching populated place or facility in the Nile Delta/Kafr El Sheikh area.

end.name: Talkha Distribution Station, Talkha, Dakahlia Governorate, Egypt (GASCO gas metering/distribution station serving the Talkha power plant and fertilizer complex)
end.coord_basis: Coordinates for the co-located Talkha CCGT power plant (Global Energy Observatory) used as a proxy anchor for the 'Talkha Distribution Station' named in the Egypt Oil & Gas pipeline table — same industrial hub in Talkha, Dakahlia; not necessarily the exact metering-station coordinates

prior_research.sheet_conflicts: GEM sheet length is 40 km; the Egypt Oil & Gas 'Guide to the Nile Delta's Oil and Gas Resources' (Feb 2020) pipeline table gives 'Abu Madi-Talkha I' as Abu Madi -> Talkha Distribution Station, 35 km, 12 in — a length discrepancy worth flagging (not corrected here; out of scope for this endpoints-only task, but the route/endpoints themselves are corroborated).
prior_research.notes: Route and existence are corroborated by TWO independent sources: Oil & Gas Journal (1996, describing the original 1975-installed 12-in 40-km 'Abu Madi field to a power plant and fertilizer plant at Talkha' line) and Egypt Oil & Gas's Feb-2020 industry-guide pipeline table (explicit 'Abu Madi-Talkha I': From=Abu Madi, To=Talkha Distribution Station, 35 km, 12 in — matching diameter, confirming this is the same line OGJ describes) and Egypt Oil & Gas's separate 2016 feature listing 'Abu Madi-Talkha I & II' among the Nile Delta's 10 main trunk pipelines. The END point (Talkha) is well anchored to a real industrial hub. The START point (Abu Madi) could not be given an independently sourced coordinate — no named town, village, or facility called 'Abu Madi' is publicly geocodable (checked OSM/Nominatim, GeoNames-style search, Wikipedia) distinct from the geological formation of the same name, which spans a much wider area including unrelated offshore fields. Set resolved:false on that basis; a human with access to Petrobel/EGPC-internal facility maps (or the GEM facility gazetteer, not citable but usable as an anchor per SOP) should be able to pin this down quickly — this is a genuinely well-documented, real pipeline, just missing a public coordinate for one endpoint.

end.name: SEGAS LNG plant (Union Fenosa Gas / Egyptian-Spanish Gas Company liquefaction complex), New Damietta, Damietta Governorate, Egypt
end.coord_basis: Global Energy Observatory facility record giving explicit coordinates for the SEGAS LNG plant; matches (within ~1 km) the prior-suggestion anchor and Wikipedia/Offshore Technology's placement of the complex in New Damietta

prior_research.notes: END point is well corroborated (2+ independent public sources: Wikipedia, Offshore Technology, Global Energy Observatory; Eni's Mar-2021 press release confirms the plant's gas supply was restored via pipeline in 2021, consistent with this line's likely tie-in date). No independently public source (EGAS, GASCO, Egyptian/international press, Eni, Wikipedia, Arabic press) names the specific take-off/metering station for the 12 km grid tie-in itself — only the general 'national gas grid' framing survives. A different, unrelated ~50 km 'El Gamil-Damietta Pipeline' (El Gamil station, Port Said, to the Damietta LNG station) was found in passing (marefa.org) — confirms GASCO runs multiple named feeder lines into this same LNG complex, supporting the plausibility of a separate short 12 km duplication line as GEM's sheet suggests, but that specific line/station is not independently nameable. Sheet StartLocation='Damietta'/EndLocation='Damietta' are technically correct at governorate/city level (not wrong, just uninformative) — no spelling_fix needed. Recommend treating the end as high-confidence and the start as a corridor placeholder only (New Damietta urban area, ~6-7 km from the SEGAS coordinates, consistent with a 12 km line) pending a human sourcing the exact GASCO station name.

start.name: Faramid / Faramid South gas field, East Obayed concession, Western Desert, Egypt
start.coord_basis: No direct geocodable point exists for the Faramid/East Obayed field itself. Coordinate is derived by offsetting 30 km on a bearing of 315 degrees (northwest) from the geocoded village of Meleiha (OSM node 11302432044, 30.7753N 27.1108E), per multiple independent press reports stating the Faramid South discovery sits in the East Obayed concession '30 km northwest of the Meleiha concession.' Concession-scale precision only (+/- ~10-20 km), not a wellhead-precise fix.

end.name: Badr El Din (BAPETCO) -- name-matched but likely NOT the correct physical facility for this pipeline; see notes
end.coord_basis: OSM node 5071716019, a road junction explicitly named 'Badr El Din' on the Qattara road near Abu Gharadig, Matrouh governorate -- consistent with descriptions of the Badr El Din (BED) oil/gas complex as ~300 km west of Cairo, on the edge of the Qattara Depression. However this point is ~159 km from the derived start point, irreconcilable with the pipeline's 38 km sheet length -- flagged low-confidence, not adopted as the final answer.

spelling_fixes.StartLocation: Faramid (Faramid South) gas field, East Obayed concession, Western Desert, Egypt

prior_research.sheet_conflicts: Sheet length is 38.0 km. The only literal, well-documented, geocodable place named 'Badr El Din' (the BAPETCO flagship BED oil/gas complex near Abu Gharadig, Matrouh governorate) is ~159 km great-circle distance from the derived Faramid/East Obayed start point -- a 4x mismatch that cannot be a 38 km pipeline. This means 'Badr El Din Company' in the sourcing (Egypt Oil & Gas: 'extending another line from the Faramid field to Badr El Din Company to process 24 mcf/d') most plausibly refers to BAPETCO the corporate operator (whose name derives from its Badr El Din field), not the distant Badr El Din facility itself. BAPETCO's own concession list separately includes Badr el Din, North East Abu Gharadig, Obaiyed, Sitra, and Matruh as distinct concessions, and a 'BAPETCO Obaiyed Gas Plant' facility in Marsa Matrouh Governorate was referenced (bizmideast.com) -- geographically consistent with a 38 km tie-in from Faramid -- but that page returned HTTP 403 on url_verifier and direct fetch, so its content/coordinates could not be independently confirmed and it is NOT included as a cited source.
prior_research.notes: Start point corroborated by 3+ independent outlets (Rigzone, NSEnergy, World Oil, plus a Zacks search snippet) describing the Faramid South discovery as sitting in the East Obayed concession, ~30 km NW of the Meleiha concession -- consistent with the prior_suggestion. Coordinate is a computed offset from the geocoded village of Meleiha (OSM), so concession-scale, not wellhead-precise. End point: the pipeline-connection claim itself (Faramid -> 'Badr El Din Company', 24 mcf/d, matching the sheet's implied ~24-25 MMcf/d) is directly and independently sourced (Egypt Oil & Gas, citing Agiba Petroleum/EGAS investment plans) so the NAME is solid, but the corresponding PHYSICAL location is ambiguous -- the only citable, geocodable 'Badr El Din' place is BAPETCO's namesake field/complex near Abu Gharadig, which is geographically incompatible (159 km) with a 38 km pipeline from Faramid. The likelier physical destination is a nearer BAPETCO-operated facility in the Obaiyed/Matrouh concession cluster (same company, same corporate branding), but no verifiable, url_verifier-passing public source could pin down that facility's precise location within the research budget available. Set resolved:false and flagged for a follow-up pass focused specifically on locating BAPETCO's Obaiyed-area gas plant/tie-in point (try BAPETCO/Shell Egypt annual reports, EGAS concession maps, or imagery around the Meleiha/East Obayed cluster for a labeled gas facility) before drawing a two-point route -- a route to the distant Abu Gharadig Badr El Din point would misrepresent the pipeline's actual geometry by roughly 4x.
